pages.heading:
The Bellweather Courier — Thursday, November 19, 1936
ELEVEN MISSING FROM VALE ESTATE
pages.placeholder: halftone press photo: Vale Manor at dusk, deputies with lanterns on the drive
pages.text:
Sheriff's deputies and volunteers from three counties searched the grounds of the Vale estate on Meridian Road for a second day yesterday without finding any trace of the eleven persons who attended a private dinner there on Monday evening.

Among the missing are Mr. and Mrs. Edmund Vale, Mr. Walter Vale and Miss Beatrice Vale; Judge Cornelius Hawthorne; Mr. Silas Blackwood; Dr. Julian Whitmore; Mr. Reginald Ashcroft of the Ashcroft Bank; the Rev. Thaddeus Bell; Mr. Anselm Mercer; and the Vale housekeeper, Mrs. Ada Pell.

Sheriff Coyle told the Courier that the clock in the dining hall stopped at 2:17 a.m., which he believes marks a failure of the house's electrical supply. "Every door was found unlocked," the Sheriff said. "There is no indication of violence." The river and the old Blackwood workings are being dragged.

The Vales' only child, Arthur, aged seven, was at school in Portland and is in the care of the family's attorneys, Messrs. Hawthorne & Mercer, who ask the public for discretion.
